claim: The Anuradhapura-period maritime system was multi-port rather than dependent on a single gateway: Mantai/Mahatittha was a major north-western entrepot, Jambukolapattana served northern embarkation and landing, Gokanna connected the east coast to Bay of Bengal traffic, and Godavaya anchored a southern route; the importance and function of each port changed over time.
bounded_by: Do not treat the four named ports as equally important, simultaneously dominant, or as four literal cardinal-point outlets controlled by a single centralized port policy throughout the full Anuradhapura period. Jambukola's Ashokan/Sanghamitta episodes are chronicle traditions and should not be recast as archaeological proof. Gokanna's growing relevance to Polonnaruwa is well supported, but a precise seventh-century trade shift causing the capital transfer is not established here.
notes: Run48 qualifies the higher-resolution museum-map reading. The robust proposition is multi-facade maritime connectivity of an inland hydraulic polity, not a static four-port state system. Mantai remains the strongest archaeologically documented long-duration entrepot among these anchors.
